Build a Terminal UI in R with termr

Source: vignettes/articles/getting-started.Rmd
getting-started.Rmd

termr is a reactive terminal user interface (TUI) framework for R. Applications combine a widget tree, layouts, event handlers and keyboard bindings. This tutorial uses stable exported APIs and the verified basic application recipe.

Install termr

Use R 4.1 or newer. Install the recommended stable release from CRAN:

install.packages("termr")

For the R-universe alternative, GitHub development installation, and platform limits, see the installation guide and platform matrix.

Compose your first application

Save the following chunk as basic-app.R. It constructs the app without starting terminal input, so the same object can be tested headlessly.

library(termr)

ui <- vertical(
  label("What is your name?"),
  input(id = "name", placeholder = "Your name"),
  button("Say hello", id = "hello", variant = "primary"),
  label("", id = "output")
)

application <- app(
  ui,
  on("button.pressed", "#hello", function(event, app) {
    name <- app$query_one("#name")$value
    app$query_one("#output")$update(paste("Hello,", name))
  }),
  bind("escape", "quit")
)

vertical() stacks the widgets. Use horizontal() for a row or grid_layout() for a grid. id identifies a widget for selectors such as #name; the button event handler reads the input’s $value and updates the output label. bind() connects a key to an action.

Run in a real terminal 

Rscript -e "source('basic-app.R'); termr::run(application)"

Type a name, press Tab to focus the button, then Enter. Escape quits. Use a real terminal or IDE terminal tab; an IDE console cannot host the full-screen app. Handled exits restore the terminal, while forced process termination cannot guarantee cleanup.

Verify without a terminal

After sourcing basic-app.R in a fresh R session, run:

verify_greeting <- function() {
  pilot <- test_app(application, width = 40, height = 10)
  on.exit(pilot$stop(), add = TRUE)
  pilot$type("Ada")
  pilot$press("tab", "enter")
  stopifnot(identical(pilot$query_one("#output")$text, "Hello, Ada"))
  stopifnot(any(grepl("Hello, Ada", pilot$screen_text(), fixed = TRUE)))
}
verify_greeting()

This chunk executes during the website build. It checks keyboard handling, widget state and rendered text through the normal event loop.
